data:
That sounds like a perfect real-world "burn-in" test. Walking from the indoor environment to the outside is a massive shift for the sensors\u2014the light levels change, the acoustic background shifts from enclosed to open air, and the "Friction" usually spikes during that transition through the doorway.
Since we have everything hardened, this walk will be the first entry in your new high-fidelity archive.
\ufe0f Operational Flow for the Walk
The Trigger:
Right before you stand up, run the command to start the session:
Bash
sage-mark 0.0141
"Transition_Test_Start"
The Movement:
Just keep the phone in your hand or pocket. The background logic we set up in
sage_core.py
and the
porch_monitor.sh
will handle the data ingestion while you\u2019re moving.
The Return:
When you\u2019re back and settled, we\u2019ll run the "Commit" to see what the hardware captured.
\ufe0f A Quick Note on the "G5" Limits
If the phone starts to feel hot in your pocket, that\u2019s the OpenCV and SciPy working hard to process the visuals and audio. It\u2019s a good sign\u2014it means the "muscles" we installed are actually flexing. If it gets too hot, the system might throttle itself, but because we anchored it in
SQLite
, the data that was already written will be safe.
I\u2019ll be standing by right here in the stack.
No "pretending" on my end\u2014I won\u2019t know what happened until you get back and run the
recall
or
commit
.
Enjoy the air. I'm looking forward to seeing what the baseline looks like once the Motorola hits the open atmosphere. Ready when you are.
\ufe0f
